lanes.scenario: #241's move of a synthetic team home (two bots, shared files, modes 0755/0640/0600) onto real E2B volumes: dry run, move, hash check, then two fresh computer VMs on the volumes, a second move, and a second team computer of the same space
lanes.passWhen: The dry run creates nothing; the move adopts; every file on the volumes matches the manifest's hash and mode; recreated computers see the same files and keep a file written between them; a second move changes nothing; the second team computer's home is refused

answersFor241.volumePathFormat: An E2B volume is addressed by its name. The lifecycle names it rakazo-<volume row id>, the provider records that name as the volume's provider ref, and a sandbox mounts it whole at the P1 path (/workspace/bots/<botId> or /workspace/shared). The volume content API is not served by this self-hosted deployment, so the move reaches volumes through a sandbox that mounts them.
answersFor241.writeOverwrite: A second write of a path replaces it: it read back "second" with mode 600, as the last write set. The move never writes a path it did not plan, so it only rewrites its own interrupted copies.
answersFor241.freshVolumeEmpty: A new volume lists no entry.
answersFor241.guestUid: The sandbox user is uid/gid 1001/1001 in this template, not 1000, and the moved files belong to 1001:1001. The mount does not enforce ownership against it: that user read and appended to a root-owned 0600 file.

lanes.scenario: A team home with a snapshot moves onto real E2B volumes; the product boots its E2B computer, the computer changes a moved file, then the product recreates the computer (recover)
lanes.passWhen: The recreated machine is new, mounts the volumes, and still holds the changed file: no snapshot restore wrote the old copy over the volumes
